topic_title: Mitigating Positional and Permutation Biases in Large Models
topic_summary: Recent research papers introduce novel methods to address positional and permutation biases in multimodal and language models. These techniques—such as shared positions, attention-only distillation, and Exchangeable Self-Distillation—help models overcome issues like the lost-in-the-middle curve and permutation sensitivity without requiring gold answers.
topic_key_facts: [Webpage] The paper on reducing permutation sensitivity categorizes permutation bias phenomena into four representative scenarios. [Webpage]
[Webpage] Exchangeable Self-Distillation (ExSD) trains a small adapter on shuffled contexts to reproduce a model's answer when reading the answer document alone. [Webpage]
[Webpage] ExSD requires no gold answers and only a few thousand examples, tested across six models starting from size 1.5. [Webpage]
[Hugging Face] The DiLE framework combines task guidance with on-policy retrieval feedback to preserve discriminative evidence in universal multimodal embeddings. [Hugging Face]
